story: Jolie Holland is a Texas-born songwriter whose 2003 debut, Catalpa, made the San Francisco Chronicle's list of the year's best albums. She played Pickathon in 2005 and 2008, and again in 2014, the year of Wine Dark Sea, her sixth solo album, self-produced and released on Anti-. Wildflower Blues followed in 2017, and in autumn 2026 she toured the Southwest, with stops in California, Arizona and New Mexico.
artist_reel_line: An autumn 2026 Southwest tour took her through California, Arizona and New Mexico.

intro: A Brooklyn singer who builds ambient music from looped voice.
story: Julianna Barwick is a Louisiana-born, Brooklyn-based singer who builds ambient music from looped voice, starting with The Magic Place in 2011. Nepenthe, recorded in Iceland with the producer Alex Somers, with her mother singing on it, came out on Dead Oceans in 2013, and she played Pickathon in 2014. Will followed in 2016 and Healing Is a Miracle in 2020. She has since teamed with the harpist Mary Lattimore on Tragic Magic for InFiné.
artist_reel_line: She made Tragic Magic with harpist Mary Lattimore and toured North America.

intro: Aaron Livingston's smoky blues and soul.
story: Son Little is Aaron Livingston, a Philadelphia musician who first drew notice singing with The Roots and RJD2. The Things I Forgot EP came out on Anti- in November 2014, the year he played Pickathon, and the self-titled debut followed in 2015; NPR called it nu-soul rather than neo-soul. New Magic came in 2017 and aloha in 2020. After a quiet stretch he returned in early 2026 with the single In Orbit and a long North American and European tour.
artist_reel_line: In Orbit, his first single in three years, came with a long 2026 tour.

intro: A Brooklyn punk band that shapeshifts.
story: The Men are a Brooklyn band formed in 2008 whose shapeshifting punk runs between noise-rock and heartland grit. Open Your Heart, on Sacred Bones in 2012, drew a Best New Music designation from Pitchfork, and they tore through Pickathon in 2014, the year of Tomorrow's Hits. They have stayed fiercely independent, on the UK label Fuzz Club with New York City in 2023 and Buyer Beware in 2025.
artist_reel_line: New York City came in 2023, then Buyer Beware in 2025, both on Fuzz Club.
